calendar.settings.added: Subscription added. Its events appear in the daily note.
calendar.settings.dailyAddField: Add the calendar to the daily template
calendar.settings.dailyFieldAdded: Added. New daily notes will list the day's events.
calendar.settings.dailyHasField: Your daily note template has the calendar field: a new daily note lists the day's events.
calendar.settings.dailyNoField: Your daily note template has no calendar field, so events do not appear yet.
calendar.settings.dailyNoNote: There is no daily note for today yet ({path}). It gets the events when it is created.
calendar.settings.dailyNoSubs: Add a subscription first: there is nothing to show.
calendar.settings.dailyRefreshed: Today's note ({path}) is refreshed: {n} lines from your calendars.
calendar.settings.fail.auth: The server refused the user name or password.
calendar.settings.fail.cors: The server did not answer this app. It may not allow Lumen's address (CORS); the desktop app is not affected.
calendar.settings.fail.no-account: Set up a CalDAV account first.
calendar.settings.fail.not-found: There is no calendar at that address.
calendar.settings.fail.server: The server answered with an error. Try again later.
calendar.settings.forgotten: The account and its password are gone from this device.
calendar.settings.icsNone: No subscriptions yet. Paste a calendar's ICS or webcal address below.
calendar.settings.icsNote: Events from these calendars appear in the daily note when its template has the calendar field. Nothing is ever written back.
calendar.settings.inbox: Note for tasks from the server
calendar.settings.intro: Sync dated tasks with a CalDAV calendar, and show events from calendar subscriptions in the daily note. Lumen asks nothing of a server until you set it up here.
calendar.settings.noneFound: No calendars found at that address.
calendar.settings.saved: Saved. The password is in the secret store, not in settings.
calendar.settings.store.encrypted: The password is kept encrypted on this device, never in settings or an export.
calendar.settings.store.keychain: The password is kept in your system's keychain, never in settings.
calendar.settings.store.plain: This browser has no encrypted store: the password is kept apart from settings, but not encrypted.
calendar.settings.synced: Synced: {pushed} sent, {pulled} received, {conflicts} conflicts left, {errors} errors.
